_comment: Credential shapes worth waking someone up for.
This list is deliberately SHORT and prefix-anchored. Every entry is a token
format whose issuer chose a distinctive prefix, which means a match is
nearly always a real credential rather than a coincidence. There is no
entropy scoring and no generic 'long random string' rule, because the alarm
is sticky: a false positive costs a human interruption and a manual
acknowledgement, so the bar to add a pattern is 'I would want to be paged
for this at 3am', not 'this might be a secret'.
Add your own with `extra_patterns` in the config rather than editing this
file, so an update does not overwrite them.
Deliberately NOT here:
AWS secret access keys  -- 40 chars of base64 with no prefix, matching
them means matching every hash and blob
bare 'Bearer <token>'   -- the shape says nothing about whether the token
is live, and it appears in every API doc
generic high entropy    -- fires on checksums, UUIDs, minified JS, and
git object ids
JWTs are the one judgement call here. A signed three-part token is
usually a live session or access token, but id_tokens and example JWTs
are everywhere in documentation. Kept, with a length floor, and listed
last so it is the obvious one to disable first if it gets noisy:
"disabled": ["jwt"]
patterns.name: jwt
